newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss hold four suspected gunrunners to Algeria.
newsitem.headline: Swiss hold four suspected gunrunners to Algeria.

text.p: Swiss police have arrested four people suspected of running guns to Islamic fundamentalists in Algeria, federal prosecutors said on Friday.

Working with authorities in the cantons of Berne, Zurich, Lucerne, Freiburg and Vaud and with Berne city police, prosecutors raided 17 houses on Wednesday and detained four people who remain in investigative custody.

"They are suspected of buying weapons and ammunition in Switzerland, hiding them in used vehicles bound for Algeria, exporting them and thus violating the law on war materiel and cantonal regulations on arms trading," they said in a statement.
They said the operation aimed to aid the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS). Most of the suspects were Algerian, but one Swiss arms dealer was involved.

An estimated 50,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces since early 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
